question: How does the persisted Rack/rack_id relate to Rig and RigRevision?
answer_if_answered: A Rack is the mutable rig; a rig revision is the immutable snapshot (id rig-rev-{content_hash[:32]}) that a run binds to. Implemented (FR-026). Decisions doc item 12 asks only for a one-word owner confirmation.

question: runs.rack_id CASCADE vs append-only runs: which wins, and what is the retention policy?
answer_if_answered: Append-only wins. Racks are soft-deleted; runs.rack_id and patches.rack_id are RESTRICT (T022, #93). Account-level deletion policy for legacy CASCADE tables is a separate piece of OQ-10.

question: Which category set is canonical (5 vs 9) and are subtypes separate?
answer_if_answered: Five canonical categories only (Voice, Clock-Rhythm, Generative, Texture-FX, Utility); no Study padding (T023, #94, FR-012).

question: Can generic port names be used in canonical patches?
answer_if_answered: Generic jacks are resolved to declared ones; unmapped ones are marked unresolved; contradictions fail the run with a validation report (T025, #97).

question: How is the seed chosen when omitted and how is it recorded?
answer_if_answered: Default is settings.default_generation_seed = 42 when the request omits seed; the seed is stored on every patch (generation_seed) and in the IR and its hash (T033, FR-024).

question: What is CHANGELOG F3 and what are the NOT_COMPUTABLE dual-write targets?
answer_if_answered: Resolved 2026-10-27: F3 is the legacy-to-canon generate dual-write; a NOT_COMPUTABLE attempt writes no run/record/library, only the inventory revision.

question: Full run status set and the state when generation yields zero patches?
answer_if_answered: queued, running, succeeded, failed, validation_failed, all terminal; zero patches from a computable rack ends succeeded (UI says no rule fits, T034).

question: Which validation findings block SUCCEEDED vs only flag?
answer_if_answered: Blocking findings (contradictions) fail the run as validation_failed with report; non-blocking (e.g. FEEDBACK_LOOP flag, MODULE_TOMBSTONED warning) are flagged. Resolved 2026-10-28 (#97).

question: What are the readiness conditions?
answer_if_answered: Built: at least one USER_CONFIRMED module and one confirmed catalog module id. Research R5 recommends recording this as the answer. Residual optional owner choice: also require a case (nothing in the engine needs one); decisions doc item 12 asks to ratify.

options.adopt_proposed_table: Adopt the proposed table: images and their OCR text 30 days default, cap form at 90, user-initiated delete; exports bytes 1 year; ledger/audit 7 years (confirm with an accountant); overlays until user deletes or account closes; refresh tokens purged 30 days after expiry; logs 30 days; account deletion removes overlays and evidence and nulls user_id. Needs: schedule expire_image_assets (Worker cron or CI), cap the form, deletion route, migration changing legacy CASCADE ledger FKs to RESTRICT/SET NULL. Most complete; largest build.

Leave overlays, ledger and account deletion undefined for now. Smallest build; leaves account-deletion and GDPR-style erasure open.
options.shorter_images_strict: Stricter privacy posture: images and OCR 7 days default, 30 max, delete raw OCR text at expiry, plus the minimal scheduling and delete route. Lower exposure for photos of homes/people; users may lose evidence needed to re-confirm inventory.
options.status_quo_document: Document current behaviour only (30-day default, 1-365, manual CLI, expiry enforced at access time) and defer the policy. No build, but photos are never purged automatically.

reversible: easy (periods are config); hard once data is deleted or FK migration runs. Retention periods for financial records and erasure duties need a lawyer/accountant to confirm; not settled here.

question: Computation rules for the six rig scores?
answer_if_answered: Owner decided 2026-10-30 (option 2): routing_flex_score = round(1-exp(-(total_ports/module_count)/8),4) and performance_density_index = round(total_ports/total_hp,4); other four stay NOT_COMPUTABLE. Implemented in canon/rig_scores.py (T035). Caveat: only ~3 catalog modules carry io_ports, so most real rigs stay NOT_COMPUTABLE until a port-data pass.

question: How are concurrent owner and admin transitions ordered?

question: Are tier prices ($4.99/$14.99/$29.99), monthly credits (25/100/unlimited), the one-time rule ($0.20/credit, $5 min) and currency/tax ratified?
evidence: https://stripe.com/pricing (fetched 2026-11-01: 2.9%+30c domestic card; +1.5% international; +1% currency conversion; Stripe Tax Basic 0.5% or $0.50/txn via API; Billing 0.7% pay-as-you-go; dispute $15, countered $15; refunds free but original fees not returned)
https://www.splice.com/plans (Creator $4.99 first month then $19.99/mo, ~200 downloads/mo credit-based; Sounds $12.99/mo annual, ~100 downloads)
https://www.canva.com/pricing/ (Pro $144/yr, Business $250/yr per person, AI allowance multiples)

Own arithmetic: 3 credits/export = $0.60 at $0.20/credit. CORE 25 credits = $5.00 at pay-as-you-go vs $4.99 (no discount, no reason to subscribe); PRO 100 credits = $20 vs $14.99 (25% off). Stripe fee on $4.99 = $0.445 (8.9%); $14.99 = $0.735 (4.9%); $29.99 = $1.17 (3.9%); $5.00 minimum = $0.445 (8.9%) domestic, +1.5% intl.

options.A_ratify_as_is: Keep $4.99/$14.99/$29.99, 25/100/unlimited, $0.20/credit, $5 min, USD only. Fastest; but CORE has no discount vs credit packs, STUDIO unlimited is open-ended cost, and Stripe fees are ~9% on CORE/min pack. Matches 'ratify' recommendation in spec.
options.B_adjust_ladder: Keep prices, change quantities (e.g. CORE 30 credits ~ $0.166/credit, PRO 100, STUDIO capped) so each tier is cheaper per credit than packs; USD only. Gives subscription incentive; owner must pick numbers.
options.C_credits_first: Launch only one-time credit packs (min raised to ~$10 to cut fee share to ~6%); defer tiers and prices for them. Matches OPEN_DECISIONS 'A first once launch date'. Less recurring revenue, fewer open questions.
options.D_regional_tax: Ratify A or B plus Stripe Tax (0.5% or $0.50/txn) and multi-currency pricing. Most compliant, adds fee (+1% conversion) and tax registration work; heavy for pre-launch.

question: What is the refund/chargeback/dispute flow, and can a balance go negative?
evidence: https://stripe.com/pricing (fetched 2026-11-01: 2.9%+30c domestic card; +1.5% international; +1% currency conversion; Stripe Tax Basic 0.5% or $0.50/txn via API; Billing 0.7% pay-as-you-go; dispute $15, countered $15; refunds free but original fees not returned)
backend/canon/exports.py (failed export reversal; never below zero, per research R7)

options.A_reverse_unspent: On provider refund reverse only unspent credits, record remainder unresolved for operator, never negative, never revoke referral reward. Matches spec recommendation; simple, may leave small loss.
options.B_allow_negative: Refund claws back full credits; balance may go negative and blocks spending until topped up. Fair to merchant, but requires new ledger rule and support handling.
options.C_manual_only: All refunds/chargebacks become unresolved events handled by operator via admin tool (T048b). Safest initially, no automation; operator load and delay.
options.D_no_refund_auto: Refund in Stripe does nothing to credits; chargebacks flagged only. Simplest, but leaves credits spendable after money returned.

question: Does a subscription payment count as the referral 'first paid purchase', and is it recorded as Purchase, Grant or both?

options.A_both: First paid invoice records a provider-verified Purchase via record_purchase(payment_verified=True) and the period credits are a separate Grant. Matches spec recommendation; referral rewards work for subscribers.
options.B_grant_only: Subscriptions never count; only one-time packs qualify. Simpler; subscribers never trigger referral rewards.
options.C_purchase_only: Record Purchase for invoices and derive credits from it, no Grant. Conflates money and entitlement; conflicts with period-grant key design.

question: Which provider subscription statuses must be distinguished and what entitlement does each give?

options.A_stripe_mapping: Per research table: active/trialing -> paid tier; past_due -> keep tier during retries, no new grant; unpaid/incomplete/incomplete_expired/canceled/paused -> FREE; grant only on invoice.paid. Matches spec recommendation and Stripe guidance.
options.B_strict: past_due also drops to FREE immediately. Less exposure to non-payers, harsher on card-retry cases.
options.C_two_state: Only active vs not active (current spec baseline). Simplest; ignores past_due grace and trialing.

question: How do upgrades/downgrades/proration affect stored tier and per-period grant?

options.A_next_period_no_proration: Store tier from the provider price on every update; new tier credits granted at next period; no proration. Matches spec recommendation; simplest, mid-period upgrade gets no extra credits.
